findings.title: Plugin request completion logs drop traceID
findings.body: logRequest used to add traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext before emitting "Plugin Request Completed". That argument was removed, and ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext does not put it back (it only sets endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname). The plugin tracing middleware does not store traceID as a log contextual attribute either, so Logger.FromContext will not restore it. Completion logs, including alerting and other non-HTTP plugin calls, can no longer be correlated with the span started for the request.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards the logger under test
findings.body: FromContext ignores both the receiver and the context and returns NewTestLogger(), a fresh instance whose Logs are not the caller's. LoggerMiddleware now records every completion exclusively via logger.FromContext(ctx).Info, so a test that injects *TestLogger and asserts InfoLogs, ErrorLogs, or contextual fields will see no calls even when a request was logged. The fake should return itself, or a child that writes into the same Logs and exposes contextual attributes.

findings.title: Moved request log fields have no test coverage
findings.body: pluginId, endpoint, datasource identity, and user were removed from LoggerMiddleware's explicit log parameters and are now supposed to arrive via ContextualLoggerMiddleware plus Logger.FromContext. Nothing in this change tests that path: there is no test for the new middleware, and metrics_middleware_test.go only renames the metrics constructor. A mis-ordered middleware stack or a FromContext implementation that drops those attributes would ship without failing CI, which is how traceID was already dropped.
